home.title: My thoughts
home.emptyBody: When a thought bothers you, write it down here. We can look at it together, slowly.

step1.title: What's the thought?
step1.hint: Write it down the way it sounds in your head.
step1.placeholder: e.g. "I'm going to mess up the presentation."

step2.title: How much do you believe this thought right now?

step3.title: Look at the evidence
step3.hint: What supports the thought, and what doesn't? Rate how convincing each point is.

step4.title: Do you perceive some of these thinking patterns in your thought?
step4.hint: Tap a pattern to read more. Select the ones that fit, or none.

step5.title: A more balanced view
step5.alternativePlaceholder: What would be a more balanced way to see this?

step6.title: How much do you believe it now?
step6.rerate: How much do you believe the original thought now?
step6.alternativeBelief: How much do you believe the alternative thought? (optional)

complete.title: Well done
complete.body: You took the time to look at this thought from a different angle. That's real practice.

detail.title: Thought
detail.exportError: The file couldn't be shared. Please try again.

all_or_nothing.name: All-or-nothing thinking
all_or_nothing.description: Seeing things in black and white, with no middle ground.
all_or_nothing.example: "If it isn't perfect, it's a total failure."

overgeneralisation.name: Overgeneralisation
overgeneralisation.description: Taking one event as proof of a never-ending pattern.
overgeneralisation.example: "I got rejected again. This always happens to me."

mental_filter.name: Mental filter
mental_filter.description: Focusing on one negative detail and ignoring everything else.
mental_filter.example: "Someone frowned during my talk, so it went badly."

disqualifying_positive.name: Disqualifying the positive
disqualifying_positive.description: Dismissing good things as if they don't count.
disqualifying_positive.example: "They only said it was good to be nice."

mind_reading.name: Mind reading
mind_reading.description: Assuming you know what others think, without real evidence.
mind_reading.example: "She didn't reply, so she must be annoyed with me."

fortune_telling.name: Fortune telling
fortune_telling.description: Predicting that things will turn out badly, as if it were a fact.
fortune_telling.example: "I just know the interview will go wrong."

catastrophising.name: Catastrophising
catastrophising.example: "If I make a mistake, I'll lose my job and everything will fall apart."

magnification_minimisation.name: Magnification / minimisation
magnification_minimisation.description: Blowing up the negatives and shrinking the positives.
magnification_minimisation.example: "My mistake was huge; my success was just luck."

emotional_reasoning.name: Emotional reasoning
emotional_reasoning.description: Believing something is true because it feels true.
emotional_reasoning.example: "I feel useless, so I must be useless."

should_statements.name: "Should" statements
should_statements.description: Rigid rules about how you or others should, must or ought to be.

labelling.name: Labelling
labelling.description: Attaching a fixed, global label to yourself or others.

personalisation_blame.name: Personalisation / blame
personalisation_blame.description: Taking all the responsibility, or putting it all on someone else.
personalisation_blame.example: "The party was boring because of me."

dictation.error: Dictation stopped. You can keep typing.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.empty: No reminders yet. A gentle reminder can help you build the habit.
reminders.permissionDenied: Notifications are turned off for this app. You can allow them in your device settings.
reminders.notificationBody: If a thought is on your mind, you can write it down now. No pressure.

settings.title: Settings
settings.privacyNote: Everything you write is stored only on this device.
settings.deleteAllBody: All thoughts and reminders will be permanently deleted from this device. This can't be undone.

page1.title: Hi, I'm here to help you slow down
page1.body: Some thoughts pop up automatically and feel very true. This app helps you write them down and look at them more closely.

page2.title: How a thought challenge works
page2.body: Write the thought, rate how much you believe it, look at the evidence for and against, spot thinking patterns, and find a more balanced view.

page3.title: Private and on your device
page3.body: There's no account. Everything you write stays on this device and is never sent anywhere.
page3.disclaimer: This app supports CBT practice. It does not replace a therapist or professional help.
page3.crisis: If you are in crisis or thinking about harming yourself, please contact your local emergency services or a crisis line right away.
